entry: suppressed-evidence C2; texas-sharpshooter C1; no cross-family tie-break (omitted evidence vs multiple testing vs chance)
fix: Add a cherry-picking entry for selection in plain view (move the "cherry-picking" alias from suppressed-evidence) and a selective-evidence tie-break; see FIXES F2. Key: also accept Texas sharpshooter here, or drop it at P001, so the two passages are graded alike.
rationale: Both flag correctly. Contrary data ("burglaries rose overall") is stated, so suppressed-evidence C2 ("omitted") fails on a literal reading; B therefore moved to texas-sharpshooter, A stretched C2. Neither label is clean. The key accepts Texas sharpshooter at P001 for the same move (hits picked after the fact, misses ignored) but not here, so it is internally inconsistent.

entry: ambiguity family rule (syllogism middle term -> four terms); redirect ambiguous-middle
fix: Key: accept four terms (quaternio terminorum) as equivalent. Catalog: in the ambiguity family rule say "report as equivocation (four terms when analysed as a categorical syllogism)", so vanilla readers see the familiar name; see FIXES F14.
rationale: Reviewers followed the catalog rule exactly; four terms caused by a shifting middle term is equivocation (the catalog redirect says so). The key is too narrow. Scored as an acceptable label; a literal string match would count it wrong.

entry: slippery-slope C3 and look-alike "well-supported chains are reasonable"; METHOD (b) hedges
fix: slippery-slope: add "evidence for the first link does not support later links; a hedge (probably) lowers the claimed probability but does not supply a missing link"; add look-alike/contrast: "where each later step needs a fresh decision by the same body, it is not likely unless a binding mechanism (precedent rule, legal duty) is shown" (contrast P112). See FIXES F4.
rationale: The evidence (3 applications in a month) supports only the first link. Applications -> approvals -> a row blocking sidewalks gets no reason, and the council itself controls every later approval. C3 ("at least one step given no adequate reason") is met; A let the hedge and first-link evidence cover the whole chain. B (possible issue) is defensible; flag is also defensible. The key's lean is right.

entry: circumstantial-ad-hominem C3 ("showing false" vs "reason to check")
fix: Add to C3/look-alikes: withholding trust in testimony = look-alike (no issue); declaring the claim false or ignorable, or refusing to examine its evidence = flag; bare "I don't trust his conclusions" about a report with its own evidence = possible issue, settle by whether the evidence is examined. See FIXES F5.
rationale: "I don't trust his conclusions" is neither "false" nor "check it". Possible issue is the correct output for this passage; the fix makes it codified rather than improvised.

entry: anecdotal-evidence C2 ("one or a few personal stories"), C3 (outside fact) and text_detectable: yes
fix: Mark anecdotal-evidence text_detectable: partly with C3 named as the outside-text condition; widen C2 to "one or a few stories, or unsystematic personal impressions"; add look-alike "long, systematically recorded professional observation". Key: drop confirmation bias from acceptable names (catalog makes it question-only) and accept possible issue as the right answer, since the counter-evidence (lunar studies) is outside the text. See FIXES F1, F13.
rationale: The passage states a generalization from experience with no explicit inference; the case against it is the outside literature. Under a text-only method possible issue is correct. The key's lean depends on outside facts.

entry: observational-interpretation C3 (binary "not addressed"; no hedge clause, unlike cum-hoc C3)
fix: Reword C3: "Confounders or reverse causation are not adequately addressed, and the causal claim is stated as established." Add: "partial adjustment + hedged causal claim -> possible issue; name the unaddressed alternative (here reverse causation / healthy-user)". See FIXES F11.
rationale: Two confounders adjusted, reverse causation open, "probably". METHOD (b) says to read hedges as hedges; the key's line between "probably" (fallacy) and "may" (legit) is too fine to be a flag. Possible issue is the better answer.

entry: hasty-generalization C3 ("too small"), no effect-size or decision look-alike
fix: Add look-alike: "a small sample with a large, consistent effect, used for a reversible or low-stakes decision"; point to unrepresentative-sample when the doubt is how the sample was chosen. With it, P042 -> no issue (matches key). See FIXES F12.
rationale: Both reviewers saw the right considerations (11/12, reversible) but the entry gave no way to act on them.

entry: appeal-to-nature C1 ("called natural") and look-alike; naturalism family pointer to is-ought
fix: C1: "called natural or an equivalent (evolved, ancestral, what our bodies were made for)". Add look-alike: "evolutionary history offered as evidence of physiological fit for a conclusion about fit". Add pointer: if the conclusion is moral/best, use is-ought or appeal-to-nature as fits. Key: under METHOD (b) charity the nutritional reading wins, so possible issue (or no issue) is defensible; a lean-fallacy key conflicts with the method. See FIXES F13.
rationale: "Appropriate" is ambiguous between nutritional fit (evolution is real evidence) and right/best. The key picks the normative reading; the method instructs the charitable one.

entry: middle-ground look-alike "practical way to reach agreement" vs C2 "concluded to be correct"
fix: Split the look-alike: midpoint offered as a settlement both sides can accept ("let's settle at 4%") = look-alike; midpoint asserted to be correct, fair, safe or true with being-in-the-middle as the only reason = C2 met. With it, P107 -> flag (matches key), P085 -> flag, P033 -> no issue. See FIXES F3.
rationale: "So a 4% raise is the fair outcome" makes a merit claim whose only support is the midpoint. Both reviewers saw this but the look-alike was too vague to rule out.
